skill.name: gcp-cloud-run
skill.description: Guides production-ready Google Cloud Run services and functions, including containers, Pub/Sub, Cloud SQL, secrets, concurrency, cold starts, and runtime limits.
skill.summary: Build and troubleshoot resilient serverless applications on Google Cloud Run.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: All 164 static matches are false positives caused by Markdown fences, illustrative template literals, and benign cloud configuration examples. Three semantic risks remain in the examples: unauthenticated Pub/Sub processing, callback URL SSRF, and reflected HTML injection.

remediation.suggestion: Configure an authenticated push service account and validate the OIDC token, audience, issuer, and identity before processing messages.
Allowlist HTTPS callback hosts, reject private and link-local addresses after DNS resolution, and avoid returning sensitive results to caller-selected destinations.
Return JSON or explicit plain text, or escape untrusted values before placing them in an HTML response.

static_findings.snippet: Message: Global mutable state may cause issues with concurrent requests.
- Containers should start fast and be stateless
- user needs AWS serverless -> aws-serverless (Lambda, API Gateway, SAM)

semantic_findings.title: Unauthenticated Pub/Sub Message Processing
semantic_findings.description: The push handler treats message shape as verification but validates no OIDC token, audience, issuer, or service account. A public endpoint could accept forged events.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The subscription example configures no authenticated push identity, and the handler checks only for a message field before processing.

semantic_findings.title: User-Controlled Callback URL Enables SSRF
semantic_findings.description: The endpoint accepts callback_url from request data and posts processing results without validating scheme, host, or resolved IP. Attackers could target internal services.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The caller directly controls the URL passed to httpx, and no allowlist or network-range validation appears before the outbound request.

semantic_findings.title: Reflected HTML Injection in HTTP Example
semantic_findings.description: The HTTP function inserts a query or body value into res.send without escaping it. Express can treat string responses as HTML and render attacker input.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The source and response sink are adjacent and contain no output encoding or explicit plain-text content type.

content.value_statement: Cloud Run projects often fail on scaling, startup, networking, and resource constraints. This skill provides deployment patterns and troubleshooting guidance for resilient serverless services.
actual_capabilities: Designs Cloud Run services and event-driven functions for Node.js and Python workloads.
Provides Dockerfile, Cloud Build, and gcloud deployment patterns.
Explains Pub/Sub, Cloud Tasks, Cloud SQL, and Secret Manager integrations.
Tunes cold starts, concurrency, CPU allocation, memory, and instance scaling.
Diagnoses runtime constraints involving temporary storage, VPC connections, startup, and request timeouts.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples but does not deploy or inspect GCP resources automatically.
Example names, regions, endpoints, and credentials require environment-specific replacement.
Security-sensitive examples require IAM, authentication, input validation, and network review.
It focuses on Google Cloud Run and does not cover equivalent AWS or Azure services.

use_cases.title: Deploy an Application Service
use_cases.description: Create a container, health endpoint, deployment configuration, and scaling plan for an existing web application.

use_cases.title: Build a Serverless Platform Pattern
use_cases.description: Connect Cloud Run with Pub/Sub, Cloud SQL, Secret Manager, or Cloud Tasks using production-oriented configuration.

use_cases.title: Resolve Cloud Run Failures
use_cases.description: Investigate cold starts, memory exhaustion, connection resets, startup failures, and timeout mismatches.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Basic Deployment
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a Cloud Run deployment plan for my [language] service in [region]. Include container requirements, PORT handling, health checks, and a gcloud command.

prompt_templates.title: Create an Event Handler
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Cloud Run Function for [event source]. Include deployment settings, payload handling, retries, authentication, and failure behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Tune Performance and Cost
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this workload profile: [traffic, latency, CPU, memory]. Recommend concurrency, minimum instances, CPU allocation, memory, timeouts, and measurement steps.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Production Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess this Cloud Run architecture: [details]. Identify reliability, IAM, secret, network, database, scaling, and observability risks. Prioritize concrete remediations.

output_examples.input: Plan a Node.js API deployment with low cold-start latency.
output: Use a small production image and run as a non-root user.
Enable startup CPU boost and begin with one minimum instance.
Measure latency before adjusting concurrency, CPU, and memory.
Add readiness behavior and graceful SIGTERM handling.

output_examples.input: Explain why a service fails after writing a large temporary file.
output_examples.output: Cloud Run stores temporary files in memory. Stream the object or use Cloud Storage, then size memory for unavoidable temporary data.

output: Authenticate push delivery with a dedicated service account.
Validate the token audience and calling identity.
Return success only after durable processing.
Configure retries and a dead-letter topic.

best_practices: Measure workload behavior before changing concurrency, instance, CPU, or memory settings.
Use least-privilege service accounts and Secret Manager for sensitive configuration.
Validate authentication, inputs, retries, timeouts, and shutdown behavior before production deployment.
anti_patterns: Do not copy placeholder commands into production without reviewing project, region, identity, and exposure settings.
Do not store large working files in temporary storage without accounting for memory.
Do not accept unauthenticated events or caller-controlled callback destinations without strict validation.

faq.question: Does this skill deploy resources automatically?
faq.answer: No. It supplies implementation and command guidance that must be reviewed and run in an authorized GCP environment.

faq.question: Which runtimes are covered?
faq.answer: The examples focus on Node.js and Python, with container patterns that can support other Cloud Run runtimes.

faq.question: Does it cover Cloud Run Functions?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes HTTP, Pub/Sub, and Cloud Storage event patterns for second-generation functions.

faq.question: Can it help reduce cold starts?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers image size, startup CPU boost, minimum instances, lazy initialization, and memory or CPU sizing.

faq.question: Does it replace a security review?
faq.answer: No. IAM, public access, input validation, secret handling, and outbound network behavior require environment-specific review.

faq.question: What GCP integrations are included?
faq.answer: It covers Pub/Sub, Cloud Tasks, Cloud SQL, Secret Manager, Cloud Storage, VPC connectors, and Cloud Build.
